appraisal_events.evidence: dit-il à Swann de l'air stupide et incrédule d'un municipal à qui un inconnu demande à voir le Président de la République... Aussitôt Cottard... adopta cette opinion... que c'était chose fort peu recherchée et qui courait les rues... et même il le plaignait un peu.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly ridicules Cottard's obtuse incomprehension, comparing his stunned disbelief to a dim policeman's, then shows him credulously swinging to the opposite extreme, dismissing the Élysée connection as commonplace and even pitying Swann.

appraisal_events.evidence: il n'osa pas dire que c'était le prince de Galles... Swann qui tâchait d'effacer ce que semblaient avoir de trop éclatant, aux yeux de son interlocuteur, des relations avec le Président de la République.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator reveals that Swann's actual connections are grander still than what has already stunned Cottard, a common friend being the Prince of Wales, which he does not dare mention, reinforcing his concealed social eminence.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator explicitly frames him as stupid and incredulous, then as gullible enough to be talked out of his own correct astonishment.
His true connections are shown to exceed even what already astonished Cottard, though this fact remains privately unshared with his interlocutor.
